zh-CN.name: Paper Products Machine Operator
zh-CN.summary: Paper products machine operators operate and monitor machinery that produces paper, cardboard, tissue and other products in paper mills or manufacturing plants, performing basic maintenance and troubleshooting. This occupation falls under New Zealand's skilled migration category, allowing migration via a skilled work visa or specific pathways, but usually requires employer sponsorship.
zh-CN.forecast_note: New Zealand's paper industry is limited in scale, but demand for packaging and hygiene products is stable. Jobs are mainly located in Waikato and Bay of Plenty on the North Island. Employment growth is expected to be moderate over the next five years, with automation slowing job growth.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression usually starts from operator, and with experience can advance to senior operator, team leader, or production supervisor. Learning automation systems or mechanical maintenance skills can enhance promotion opportunities, but management positions are limited.

zh-CN.name: Crane, Hoist or Lift Operator

zh-CN.forecast_note: New Zealand's construction industry continues to grow, with large infrastructure projects (e.g., Auckland light rail, Christchurch rebuild) driving demand for crane operators. Employment growth is expected to be stable over the next 5 years, but affected by economic cycles, skilled operators remain in short supply.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Start as an assistant operator, obtain a New Zealand crane registration certificate to become an independent operator. With experience, advance to supervisor, trainer, or higher-level crane license (e.g., tower crane, mobile crane), with significant salary increases.

zh-CN.name: Boiler or Engine Operator

This occupation can lead to immigration via the Accredited Employer Work Visa (AEWV) or Skilled Migrant Category (SMC), but is not on the Green List and requires employer support.
zh-CN.forecast_note: Employment prospects for boiler or engine operators in New Zealand are stable, driven mainly by demand from manufacturing, transport, and power generation industries. Due to equipment automation and environmental regulations, job growth is slow, but experienced operators remain in demand. Expected annual growth of about 1-2% over the next five years.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression includes advancing from junior operator to senior operator, shift supervisor, or equipment maintenance manager. By obtaining New Zealand national certificates (e.g., ENP3011) and gaining experience, you can move into supervisory or technical training roles. Some operators can obtain an engineer license.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior operators can advance to senior operators or shift supervisors through internal training; some may move into equipment maintenance or quality control roles. Requires years of experience, with limited management opportunities.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Starting as an assistant dispatcher or signal operator, gaining experience to advance to senior dispatcher or control center supervisor, with some transitioning to railway planning or safety management roles. Typically takes 5-10 years to reach senior positions.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Can advance from novice operator to senior operator, team leader, or transition to forestry machinery maintenance technician. With accumulated experience, can start a business contracting logging operations.

As it is not a shortage occupation, competition is moderate, and candidates with relevant certifications and work experience have better employment prospects.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior designers can progress to senior designer, design director, or start their own studio; they may also specialize in residential, commercial, or sustainable design.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior coaches can accumulate experience and advance to senior coaches, department heads, or fitness managers, or specialize in specific areas (e.g., rehabilitation training, sports nutrition) to become independent personal trainers or open their own studios.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Progress from junior physiotherapist to senior specialist (e.g., sports injuries, neurological rehabilitation), or transition into management (e.g., department head) or academic research.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Entry-level pharmacists can advance to senior clinical pharmacist, pharmacy manager, or specialize in areas such as oncology or mental health, and can also transition into the pharmaceutical industry or academic research.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior optometrists can advance to senior optometrist, clinical supervisor, or ophthalmology clinic manager. Some specialize in areas like pediatric optometry or low-vision rehabilitation.

zh-CN.forecast_note: UK dentist demand remains strong, driven by an aging population and increased oral health awareness. NHS dental services have gaps, private dental market is growing, and employment prospects are good.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior dentists can advance to senior dentists or specialist dentists (e.g., orthodontics, oral surgery), or move into clinic management or academic research. Experienced dentists can also open private practices.

zh-CN.forecast_note: Demand for radiographers in the UK continues to grow, driven mainly by an aging population and rising cancer rates. The NHS long-term plan to increase imaging capacity means job growth is expected to be above average over the next 10 years.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior radiographers can advance to senior radiographers, clinical specialists (e.g., ultrasound, MRI), management roles, or education/research positions. Some may become consultant radiographers with independent reporting rights.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Entry-level care workers can advance to senior care workers, team leaders, or clinical specialists (e.g., critical care). They can also move into education, management, or research roles.

zh-CN.forecast_note: With an aging population and rising diabetes prevalence, foot care demand continues to grow. Both NHS and private institutions require podiatrists, with stable employment prospects, especially in community healthcare and specialist clinics.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior podiatrists can work in NHS or private clinics; with experience, they can advance to senior podiatrist, podiatry consultant, or start a private practice. They can also specialize in areas such as diabetic foot or sports medicine.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior technicians can advance to senior technicians or lab supervisors through experience, some may move to quality control or R&D roles. Further study can lead to becoming a scientist.

zh-CN.forecast_note: Demand for fishmongers and poultry processors in UK retail and food processing is stable, but automation may reduce entry-level jobs. Employment expected to decline slightly over the next five years.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Can progress from junior assistant to senior processor or supervisor. Some may move to quality control, food safety inspection, or management. Experienced workers can run their own fish stall or poultry shop.

zh-CN.name: Chefs
zh-CN.summary: Chefs plan menus and prepare food in hotels, restaurants, clubs, private residences, etc., or supervise food production. They ensure quality, taste, and presentation of dishes meet standards, while managing kitchen teams and inventory.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK hospitality industry continues to grow, with high demand for chefs, especially experienced ones. Post-Brexit, the EU workforce has decreased, leading to a local chef shortage, with projected employment growth of 5-10% over the next five years. High-end dining and chain hotels are major employers.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Usually starting as a kitchen hand or junior chef, gaining experience to become a section chef (e.g., sauce chef, pastry chef), then advancing to sous chef, head chef, or executive chef. Alternatively, move into food service management or start a restaurant.

zh-CN.name: Cooks
zh-CN.summary: Chefs in clubs, private households, fast-food outlets, live-cooking food stores, and other institutions prepare, season, and cook food, usually using pre-prepared ingredients.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK catering industry continues to develop, with stable demand for chefs. Driven by post-pandemic recovery and growth in delivery services, job opportunities are expected to remain good in the coming years. However, competition may vary by region and employer type.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior chefs can start as kitchen assistants, gain experience, and advance to supervisor or senior chef. Further progression can lead to executive chef or catering manager. Some chefs transition to advanced culinary fields through specialized training or certification.

zh-CN.name: Catering and bar managers
zh-CN.summary: Food and beverage managers plan, direct, and coordinate catering services in restaurants, bars, hotels, educational institutions, etc., managing on-site dining and takeaway operations.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK hospitality industry is gradually recovering, with employment growth expected to be about 5% from 2023 to 2033, driven by tourism and leisure, but competition remains fierce.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression path: from server or supervisor to department manager, then to food and beverage manager, operations manager, or regional manager. Some may move into self-employed restaurant ownership or consulting.

zh-CN.name: Florists
zh-CN.summary: Florists sell flowers and related products in wholesale or retail businesses, design and create bouquets, wreaths, condolence sprays, and other floral arrangements for public purchase.
zh-CN.forecast_note: Job prospects for florists in the UK are stable, driven by demand from festivals, weddings, and business events. Employment is expected to grow slightly over the next five years, but competition is strong, especially in urban areas.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Florists typically start as apprentices or assistants and can progress to senior florist or store manager with experience. Some choose to start their own flower shops or move into event planning, wedding floristry, and other specialized fields.

zh-CN.name: Sports and leisure assistants
zh-CN.summary: A Sports and Leisure Assistant provides, maintains, and supervises facilities used for sporting and recreational activities, ensuring continuity of entertainment and social activities, offering betting odds and accepting bets, controlling gambling activities, and providing backstage support in production and broadcasting enterprises to ensure smooth operations.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK sports and leisure industry has stable employment prospects, driven by increasing health awareness and major sports events, with expected slow growth in job demand. However, leisure spending may decrease due to economic fluctuations, and competition for jobs is moderate.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior assistants can advance to team supervisor or facility manager, or move into specialist areas like fitness instructor or event coordinator. Some pursue a sport science degree through further study to enter management or coaching roles.

zh-CN.name: Travel agents
zh-CN.summary: Travel advisors provide itinerary suggestions, book flights and hotels, and arrange travel packages, handling related payments. They are key contacts in the tourism industry, typically working at travel agencies or online travel platforms
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK travel advisor industry is facing digital transformation, but high-end customized and complex itineraries still require professional advisors. Employment opportunities are expected to be concentrated in travel consulting and online platforms, and those with professional certifications will have an advantage.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior travel consultant can advance to senior consultant, team leader, or travel operations manager. Also possible to become a destination specialist, corporate travel manager, or start own travel agency.

zh-CN.name: Housekeepers and related occupations
zh-CN.summary: Butlers and related workers perform housekeeping and other butler duties in private households, hotels, schools, hostels, etc., ensuring a clean and orderly environment. This occupation typically requires attention to detail, responsibility, and good time management skills.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK hospitality sector continues to recover, with steady demand for cleaning and housekeeping services in hotels, resorts, and private households. Job growth is expected to be stable in the coming years, but economic fluctuations may lead some employers to reduce full-time positions in favor of part-time or outsourced roles.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Entry-level roles are mostly cleaning or room attendants; with experience, can advance to head housekeeper, housekeeping supervisor, or hotel housekeeping manager. Some transition to private household services or start their own cleaning business. Multi-skills (e.g., cooking, nursing) help improve career ceiling.

zh-CN.forecast_note: With the growth in domestic tourism and leisure accommodation demand in the UK, the homestay industry is steadily developing. However, due to seasonal effects, some positions are part-time or seasonal. Employment is expected to grow slightly over the next 5 years.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Start in front desk or housekeeping, gain experience, then progress to owner or manager. Some operators expand by purchasing existing properties or franchising brands. Can also move into hotel management or tourism services.

zh-CN.summary: Display and sell various goods and services to customers in stores, showrooms, etc., providing consultation, checkout, stocking, and other basic retail support.
zh-CN.forecast_note: UK retail employs a large workforce, but e-commerce impacts brick-and-mortar job growth; employment expected to decline slightly from 2023-2033, with about 200,000 annual vacancies mainly replacing retirees.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career path: Senior Sales Assistant → Department Supervisor → Assistant Store Manager → Store Manager → Regional Manager. Some can transition to purchasing, merchandising, or e-commerce operations. Need to accumulate customer service and sales management experience.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression includes senior telesales representative, team leader, sales manager, etc. After gaining customer service experience, can move to other sales or account management roles.

zh-CN.forecast_note: With the digital transformation of enterprises and the prevalence of data-driven decision-making, demand for database and website management is growing steadily. The integration of cloud computing and social media management will create new jobs, with an estimated employment growth of about 10% over the next decade.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior technicians can advance to database administrator, web administrator, or social media manager. With experience, they can move into more senior roles such as data analysis, cybersecurity, or cloud architecture, or become team leaders.

zh-CN.name: Data analysts
zh-CN.summary: Data analysts collect, organize, and analyze various data to provide decision support for organizations or society.
zh-CN.forecast_note: Demand for data analysts in the UK continues to grow, especially in finance, tech, and retail. Employment growth of about 20% expected from 2023-2033, driven by big data and AI.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior data analysts can advance to senior analyst, data scientist, or analytics manager, or move into data engineering or AI fields.

zh-CN.name: Information technology trainers
zh-CN.summary: Information technology trainers provide computer usage instruction and plan/organize IT training courses in industrial, commercial, and other institutions.
zh-CN.forecast_note: With the acceleration of digital transformation, corporate demand for employee IT skills training continues to grow, and the employment prospects for this occupation are stable. The number of positions is expected to increase slightly over the next five years.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior trainers can advance to senior trainer, training manager, or learning and development supervisor; can also shift to IT consulting or instructional design roles.

occupations.name_en: Computer system and equipment installers and servicers

zh-CN.name: Computer system and equipment installers and servicers
zh-CN.summary: Responsible for installing, maintaining, and repairing computer hardware, including servers, network equipment, and PCs, ensuring system stability.
zh-CN.forecast_note: With accelerating digital transformation, the demand for IT support engineers in the UK remains stable. Although cloud computing reduces some on-site maintenance, hardware reliance persists. Job growth of about 5% is expected from 2023 to 2033, with approximately 3,000 new positions annually.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Starting from entry-level technical support, you can advance to senior engineer, team lead, or IT infrastructure manager. You can also transition to cloud computing or cybersecurity for higher salary and career growth.

zh-CN.name: Embedded / Firmware Engineer
zh-CN.summary: Embedded/firmware engineers develop underlying software on microcontrollers and SoCs, covering RTOS/bare metal, drivers, communication protocol stacks, low power consumption, and firmware security, widely used in IoT, automotive, medical, and industrial equipment, making them high-value positions at the hardware and software intersection.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the UK, device networking and automotive/medical/defense electronics are driving demand for embedded devices, with tight supply and demand for embedded/firmware engineers and a solid outlook.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Edge AI, functional safety, and device security have become hot topics in the UK, with firmware engineers skilled in low-level debugging and real-time constraints in short supply; AI-generated prototypes, but the hardware still relies on people at its core.

zh-CN.name: FPGA Engineer
zh-CN.summary: FPGA engineers use Verilog/VHDL to implement high-performance digital circuits on programmable logic devices, covering signal processing, low-latency computing, and hardware acceleration. They are mainly employed in defense aerospace, high-frequency trading, and semiconductor/telecommunications companies, where positions are scarce, barriers to entry, and salaries are attractive.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the UK, global chip autonomy and AI are accelerating the spillover of demand, FPGA engineers are scarce and supply is even scarcer, senior talent is in short supply, and salaries are at the top end of electronic engineering platforms.
zh-CN.trend_summary: The UK focuses on AI accelerators and low-power/simulation design, with engineers skilled in RTL, timing, and layout in a scarce area; AI assistance is limited, but architecture and tape-out responsibilities are highly professional.

zh-CN.name: ASIC Design Engineer
zh-CN.summary: ASIC design engineers are responsible for the digital front-end (RTL design/integration) or back-end (physical design/timing convergence) of application-specific integrated circuits, targeting SoCs, AI accelerators, and dedicated chips. These are scarce, high-threshold, and well-paid deep-tech positions.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the UK, global chip autonomy and AI demand are accelerating overflow, ASIC chip design engineers are scarce and supply is even scarcer, senior talent is in short supply, and salaries are at the high end of electronic engineering.
zh-CN.trend_summary: The UK focuses on AI accelerators and low-power/simulation design, with engineers skilled in RTL, timing, and layout in a scarce area; AI assistance is limited, but architecture and tape-out responsibilities are highly professional.

Entry-level positions (such as simple RTL modules) may be squeezed, but demand for high-end positions is growing.

zh-CN.name: Analog / Mixed-Signal IC Design Engineer
zh-CN.summary: Analog/mixed-signal IC design engineers design analog and digital-analog hybrid modules in chips, such as ADC/DAC, PLL, power management (PMIC), RF front-end, and high-speed interfaces, which are recognized as the most difficult to automate and most rely on intuitive experience in chip design, with experts in extremely scarce.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the UK, global chip autonomy and AI are accelerating the spillover of demand, making analog/mixed-signal IC design engineer positions scarce and even less available, while senior talent is in high demand and salaries are at the top end of electronic engineering.
zh-CN.trend_summary: The UK focuses on AI accelerators and low-power/simulation design, with engineers skilled in RTL, timing, and layout in a scarce area; AI assistance is limited, but architecture and tape-out responsibilities are highly professional.

zh-CN.name: IC Verification Engineer
zh-CN.summary: IC verification engineers use SystemVerilog/UVM to set up verification environments, write test platforms, and conduct coverage-driven and formal verification before chip tape-out, ensuring designs meet specifications. Verification workload usually accounts for more than half of chip development, with more positions than design positions, making it a relatively viable and high-paying path to enter the semiconductor industry.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the UK, rising chip complexity drives up verification demand, and IC verification engineers typically outnumber design positions, making it a relatively viable high-paying path into semiconductors.
zh-CN.trend_summary: UK SoC-level verification, low power consumption, and security verification are key focuses; AI improves test generation and debugging efficiency, while methodology and coverage convergence remain dominated by engineers.

zh-CN.summary: Plan, organize, direct, and coordinate the daily operations of garages and specialist vehicle repair workshops, ensuring profitability and meeting customer needs.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Can progress from senior technician or service advisor to branch manager or regional manager, or start their own garage through accumulated experience and capital.

zh-CN.name: Sheet metal workers
zh-CN.summary: Sheet metal workers use manual or machine tools to lay out, cut, shape, and join metal sheets to manufacture and repair sheet metal products and components (excluding vehicle bodies).
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK sheet metal worker market is relatively stable, supported by demand from the construction and manufacturing sectors. Employment opportunities are expected to remain steady over the next decade, with some roles reduced due to automation, but skilled tradespeople are still in demand.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Entry-level panel beaters can progress to senior technicians, supervisors, or project managers. Through NVQ/SVQ certification and extensive experience, they can also move into estimating, design, or training roles.

zh-CN.name: Metal plate workers, smiths, moulders and related occupations
zh-CN.summary: Mark, drill, shape, position, rivet, and seal metal sheets and beams to build structures and frameworks; operate power hammers and presses to shape heated metal, manufacture and repair metal products; make moulds and cores for metal casting.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK manufacturing and construction industries have stable demand for sheet metal processing and casting skills, particularly driven by infrastructure and energy projects. Apprenticeships are the main entry route; experienced workers are in short supply, and job prospects are good.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Usually start as an apprentice or junior worker, progressing to senior technician, supervisor, or quality inspector with experience. Some become mold designers or manufacturing engineers through further training, or self-employed in small metal processing plants.

zh-CN.name: Welding trades
zh-CN.summary: Welders use various equipment and techniques to join metal parts through welding, brazing, and soldering, and to cut and remove metal defects. This occupation has steady demand in manufacturing, construction, and repair services, and is among the skilled trades in shortage in the UK.
zh-CN.forecast_note: UK welding job prospects are positive, with strong demand especially in manufacturing and infrastructure projects. Energy, automotive, and shipbuilding industries continue to need qualified welders. Apprenticeships are the main entry route, and the 2024 Shortage Occupation List indicates the occupation still faces talent shortages.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression typically starts with an apprenticeship, advancing to skilled welder, then to supervisor, inspector, or welding engineer. Some enter high-paying fields such as pipeline welding or underwater welding by obtaining advanced certifications (e.g., CSWIP, ASME).

zh-CN.trend_summary: Can start as an apprentice and progress to senior plumber, supervisor, or project manager. May also specialise in gas, steam, or refrigeration pipe systems through further training.

zh-CN.name: Vehicle paint technicians
zh-CN.summary: Vehicle paint technicians apply paint, cellulose, vinyl decals, and wraps to motor vehicle bodies for protection or decoration. This role requires fine manual skills and knowledge of paint technology.
zh-CN.forecast_note: Employment prospects for vehicle paint technicians in the UK are stable, with ongoing demand due to vehicle ownership and accident repairs. New energy vehicle repairs may introduce new skill requirements, but overall job demand remains steady.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior technicians can advance through apprenticeships to senior technician, workshop supervisor, or technical trainer. Some technicians may move into vehicle damage assessment or body repair management.

zh-CN.name: Aircraft maintenance and related trades
zh-CN.summary: Install, maintain, overhaul and repair aircraft engines and components, including licensed aircraft engineers (classified under group 3113).
zh-CN.forecast_note: With the recovery of the aviation industry and growth in global flights, aircraft maintenance demand is stable. The UK Civil Aviation Authority has strict requirements for maintenance personnel, and employment is expected to remain stable
zh-CN.trend_summary: Starting as an apprentice, one can advance to a licensed aircraft engineer, then become a senior maintenance technician or team leader, or move into quality control or management roles.

occupations.name_en: Boat and ship builders and repairers

zh-CN.name: Boat and ship builders and repairers
zh-CN.summary: Shipbuilder and repairer build, install, and repair wooden hull structures and fittings, and form, position, rivet, and seal metal plates and components to create metal structures and frameworks for ships.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK shipbuilding and repair industry faces skill shortages, particularly in environmental and naval vessel upgrades. Although overall employment growth is steady, demand is high for those skilled in modern composites or welding.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression can start from an apprentice, and gradually advance to senior technician, team leader, or shipbuilding manager. Holding advanced welding or composite material certificates can lead to yacht construction or naval projects, with some moving into design or quality inspection roles.

zh-CN.summary: Responsible for the construction, assembly, repair, and commissioning of railway vehicles (such as train carriages and locomotives), ensuring safe train operation.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK rail network continues to upgrade, driven by large projects like HS2; but automation may affect some roles, overall stable.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Can progress from apprentice to senior technician or team leader; some transition to railway engineering management or quality control roles.

zh-CN.name: Electricians and electrical fitters
zh-CN.summary: Electricians and electrical assemblers are responsible for component assembly in electrical equipment manufacturing, as well as installation, maintenance, and repair of electrical installations, machinery, and appliances; they are essential skilled trades in construction and industry.
zh-CN.forecast_note: Demand for electricians in the UK continues to grow, driven by green energy transition, smart home adoption, and infrastructure upgrades, with an estimated 8% job growth over the next decade, offering good employment prospects.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career path is clear: starting as an apprentice or junior electrician, gaining experience to advance to senior electrician, supervisor, or project manager, or obtaining higher-level qualifications to become an electrical engineer or self-employed.

occupations.name_en: Tv, video and audio servicers and repairers

zh-CN.name: Tv, video and audio servicers and repairers
zh-CN.summary: TV, video, and audio repair engineers install, repair, and maintain household TV, video, and audio equipment. This is a skilled trade, usually working in electronics repair shops or home appliance service companies.
zh-CN.forecast_note: With the popularity of smart TVs and home entertainment systems, demand for TV repair engineers remains stable. However, as many devices become highly integrated, repair difficulty increases, potentially limiting employment growth. A slight decrease in jobs is expected in the coming years, but replacement demand persists.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career path: start as an apprentice or junior technician, gain experience, and advance to senior engineer or team supervisor. Some may pursue a degree in electronic engineering and transition to more complex industrial electronic repair or R&D roles.

zh-CN.summary: Responsible for maintaining and repairing household appliances, office machines, and electrical equipment to ensure safe operation of electrical systems; a key technical role for the normal functioning of homes and commercial facilities
zh-CN.forecast_note: With the renovation of old buildings and the green energy transition, demand for electrical maintenance is steadily growing. The UK electrical maintenance industry is expected to grow by about 2% annually over the next decade, with ample job opportunities.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior tradespeople can advance to senior technicians or team supervisors through apprenticeships, and with experience can move into electrical engineering management, equipment manufacturer technical consulting, or start their own business.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior steel structure installers can gain experience through apprenticeships and advance to senior installer, team leader, or project supervisor. They can also move into steel structure design or project management.

zh-CN.name: Stonemasons and related trades
zh-CN.summary: Stone masons construct and restore stone structures, cutting, shaping, and polishing granite, marble, slate, and other stone for building, decoration, and other purposes.
zh-CN.forecast_note: UK construction industry continues to develop; restoration of historic buildings and high-end residential projects create stable demand for stonemasons. Despite reduced new builds, skilled stonemasons remain in short supply.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Starting as an apprentice, can advance to senior stonemason, foreman, or specialize in stone carving restoration, monument manufacturing, etc., or start your own business.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Starting as an apprentice, you can progress to senior bricklayer, foreman, or become a self-employed contractor through experience, or move into construction management.

zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK construction industry continues to grow, with housing construction and green energy transition driving demand for plumbers. Employment is projected to grow by about 10% from 2023-2033, with around 8,000 new positions annually.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression paths include becoming a senior tradesperson, site supervisor, self-employed contractor, or starting your own company. Skills can be upgraded through NVQ Level 3 and advanced certificates to enter specialised fields such as HVAC or renewable energy.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior carpenters typically enter the trade through apprenticeships and can progress to senior carpenter, foreperson, or project manager with experience. They may also specialize in joinery, furniture making, or heritage restoration.

zh-CN.name: Construction and building trades supervisors

zh-CN.trend_summary: Practitioners can start as apprentices, gradually become skilled artisans, or move into high-end custom, restoration studio management; some may set up their own studios or enter the luxury repair field.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior craftsmen can advance to senior craftsmen or supervisors, or transition to custom furniture design, repair, or self-employment. Some become teachers or assessors through further training.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Can advance from ordinary seaman to senior seaman, boatswain, or engineer; by obtaining maritime certificates, can become captain or chief engineer.

zh-CN.name: Air transport operatives
zh-CN.summary: Responsible for aircraft refueling, loading/unloading cargo, guiding aircraft movement, and placing ramps or stairs to ensure safe passenger boarding and disembarkation. Works on the airport ground service frontline, a key support role in air transport.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The UK aviation industry continues to recover, with stable demand for air transport operations officers over the next decade. Airport expansions and flight increases will create a certain number of jobs. However, automation (e.g., auto-docking systems, self-service baggage handling) may replace some repetitive tasks, resulting in slow overall employment growth.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression paths are limited: can advance from aviation transport operator to ground supervisor or airport operations coordinator. Some transition to aircraft dispatch or aviation safety roles through internal training. Need to accumulate experience and obtain relevant certifications for career development.

zh-CN.forecast_note: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects about 6% employment growth for this occupation from 2023 to 2033, faster than average. Digital transformation and increased social media importance boost demand for PR managers, but competition is strong.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Usually start as a PR specialist or media relations assistant, gain experience to advance to senior manager, director, then to vice president or chief communications officer (CCO), or move to consulting or entrepreneurship.

zh-CN.name: Fundraising Managers

zh-CN.forecast_note: The US nonprofit sector continues to grow, with an estimated employment growth of about 8% from 2024-2034, faster than average. Digital transformation and rising donor expectations drive demand, but competition is intense.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career path typically starts as a fundraising officer or event coordinator, then progresses to fundraising manager, and then to director or vice president level. Some may transition to consulting or foundation development.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Usually promoted from administrative assistant or office manager; with experience can advance to senior administrative manager or operations director. Some may transition to facility management or procurement management.

zh-CN.name: Purchasing Managers

zh-CN.trend_summary: Common promotion path: Buyer → Procurement Supervisor → Procurement Manager → Supply Chain Director/VP. Can also move into supply chain management, operations management, or consulting. Holding CPSM certification can accelerate advancement.

zh-CN.name: Cartographers and Photogrammetrists

zh-CN.forecast_note: According to the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, employment growth from 2023 to 2033 is projected at 8%, above the average for all occupations. zh-CN.trend_summary: Entry-level positions such as GIS technician or cartographer assistant; with experience, can advance to senior cartographer or project manager. Some move to research or development roles, such as GIS developer or geospatial data scientist. Management positions like GIS director or surveying department head require extensive professional experience and management skills.

BLS projects about 5% employment growth from 2022 to 2032, but competition is high. Employment opportunities are concentrated in hospitals, specialty clinics, and academic medical centers.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career path: After completing medical school and 4 years of neurology residency, further subspecialization (e.g., epilepsy, stroke, movement disorders) and board certification. Advancement options include becoming department head, clinical research lead, or opening a private practice.

zh-CN.name: Obstetricians and Gynecologists

zh-CN.forecast_note: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects about 2% employment growth from 2023 to 2033, below average, but women's health demand is stable. Aging population and medical technology may create opportunities, but competition is fierce, especially in urban areas.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career path typically begins with residency training (4 years), after which one can become an attending physician. Further specialization in maternal-fetal medicine, reproductive endocrinology, etc., or advancement to department head or hospital management. Some enter academic research or private practice.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Career path: Medical school (4 years) → Pediatric residency (3 years) → Fellowship (e.g., pediatric cardiology, 3 years) → Attending physician. Can advance to department head, hospital administrative role, or academic researcher.

zh-CN.trend_summary: After completing residency training, start as a general psychiatrist and progress to specialties (e.g., child and adolescent, addiction, forensic psychiatry), or become a medical director, academic professor. Some may open private practices or engage in research.

zh-CN.forecast_note: Demand for nurses in the U.S. continues to grow due to aging population and expansion of emergency medical services. BLS projects 7% employment growth from 2022-2032, with approx. 20,000 annual openings.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Progress from entry-level paramedic to advanced care paramedic, further to supervisor, trainer, or emergency department management roles; some pursue a physician assistant or nursing degree.

zh-CN.name: Dietetic Technicians
zh-CN.summary: Under the supervision of a registered dietitian, assist in providing food services and nutrition programs, may plan and prepare meals according to established guidelines, teach food and nutrition principles, or provide individual counseling.
zh-CN.forecast_note: With an aging population and increase in chronic diseases, demand for nutrition services continues to grow. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects about 7% employment growth from 2023-2033, on par with the average, but demand is stable in healthcare.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Usually start as a dietary technician, gain experience to qualify as a registered dietitian, then advance to clinical dietitian or nutrition services manager. Some move into food service management or public health nutrition.

zh-CN.name: Psychiatric Technicians
zh-CN.summary: Under the direction of physicians or other health practitioners, care for individuals with mental or emotional disorders or disabilities, monitor their physical and mental condition and report to medical staff, participate in rehabilitation and treatment plans, assist with personal hygiene, and administer oral or injectable medications.
zh-CN.forecast_note: Mental health service demand in the U.S. is growing; psychiatric technician roles are projected to grow 12% in the next decade, driven by aging population, increased mental health awareness, and expansion of community treatment.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Can advance from entry-level psychiatric technician to senior technician, team leader, or become a registered nurse, mental health counselor, etc. through further education; some institutions offer internal training promotion paths.

zh-CN.name: Surgical Technologists
zh-CN.summary: Surgical technicians assist surgeons and nurses in the operating room, preparing instruments, adjusting equipment, passing tools, and ensuring a sterile environment.
zh-CN.forecast_note: U.S. surgical technologist employment outlook is favorable, with projected growth of about 6% from 2023-2033, driven mainly by an aging population and increased surgical demand.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior surgical technologists can gain experience and advance to lead surgical technologist or operating room manager, or further study to become a registered nurse or surgical assistant.

zh-CN.name: Veterinary Technologists and Technicians

zh-CN.forecast_note: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects about 20% employment growth for this occupation from 2023 to 2033, much faster than average. Increased pet spending and demand for veterinary services are key drivers.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career advancement includes obtaining professional certifications (e.g., veterinary emergency care, anesthesia technician) to specialize, or promotion to head technician, veterinary technical supervisor, veterinary clinic manager, etc.

zh-CN.name: Medical Records Specialists
zh-CN.summary: Responsible for compiling, processing, and maintaining medical records of hospital and clinic patients, including classifying diagnoses, surgeries, medical services, etc., and entering into industry-standard coding systems, ensuring compliance with medical, administrative, ethical, and legal requirements.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Start as an entry-level coder, can advance to senior coder, coding supervisor, compliance auditor, or health information manager. Some transition to medical data analysis or consulting after obtaining certifications like RHIA or CPC.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Can advance from junior optician to senior optician, store manager, or regional manager, or move into optical lab management or optometric assistant roles.

zh-CN.name: Orthotists and Prosthetists
zh-CN.summary: Orthotists and prosthetists are responsible for designing, measuring, fabricating, and fitting orthoses, prostheses, and other assistive devices to help patients restore limb function or improve quality of life. This occupation requires a combination of clinical assessment, manual fabrication, and technical application skills.
zh-CN.forecast_note: US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects employment growth for this occupation at about 15% from 2023-2033, much faster than average. Aging population and diabetes-related amputations increase demand, technological advances such as 3D printing and smart prosthetics also create new opportunities.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression includes from entry-level technician to senior clinical expert, team supervisor, or clinic manager. Some practitioners move into R&D or sales, or pursue a PhD for academic research. Certification from the American Board for Certification in Orthotics, Prosthetics & Pedorthics (ABC) is a core requirement.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Entry-level starts as an Audiometric Technician, gain experience to become a Senior Hearing Aid Specialist or Audiology Center Supervisor. Continuing education to obtain an Audiologist degree can expand into clinical audiology diagnostics and rehabilitation.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Entry-level typically starts in medical data entry or technical support, intermediate can advance to systems analyst or project manager, senior can become health information director or chief information officer (CIO).

zh-CN.name: Athletic Trainers
zh-CN.summary: Athletic trainers assess and treat musculoskeletal injuries or conditions, providing preventive, therapeutic, emergency, and rehabilitative care. They work with athletes and active individuals to prevent and rehabilitate sports-related injuries.
zh-CN.forecast_note: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics projects about 23% growth for this occupation from 2023-2033, much faster than average. With increasing public health awareness and sports participation, demand for athletic trainers is strong, especially in schools, sports teams, and rehabilitation centers.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior sports trainers typically start as assistants or interns, gain experience, and advance to lead or supervisor roles. Some move into sports medicine management, teaching, or research. Obtaining specialty certifications (e.g., orthopedics, rehabilitation) can improve promotion prospects.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior analysts can advance to senior analyst or team lead; with experience, they can move into data science, supply chain management, or become management consulting advisors.

zh-CN.name: Statisticians
zh-CN.summary: Statisticians use mathematical and statistical theory to collect, organize, interpret numerical data, providing usable information. Can specialize in biostatistics, agricultural statistics, business statistics, or economic statistics.
zh-CN.forecast_note: BLS projects 30% employment growth for statisticians from 2023-2033, much faster than average. Big data and machine learning drive demand, especially in tech, healthcare, and government.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior statisticians can advance to senior statistician, chief data scientist, or statistical manager. Also can transition to data science, machine learning engineering, or research. A PhD provides easier access to top R&D positions.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior analysts can advance to senior data scientist, chief data officer, or AI architect. They can also transition to machine learning engineer, data engineering, or management roles.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Junior hardware engineers can advance to senior engineer or project manager; may also move into chip design, system architecture, or R&D management. Professional certification (e.g., PE) helps career development.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Career progression typically moves from assistant professor to associate professor to full professor, with some transitioning to research universities or senior R&D roles in industry. Requires continuous publication and pursuit of tenure.

zh-CN.name: Radio, Cellular, and Tower Equipment Installers and Repairers

zh-CN.forecast_note: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics projects employment growth of about 4% for this occupation from 2023 to 2033, slower than the average. With the development of 5G and wireless communication technology, demand for tower installation and maintenance is stable, but automation may limit growth.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Entry-level positions typically start as tower installation or repair assistants; gain experience to advance to senior technician or supervisor, some may move to network planning or project management. Continuous learning of new technologies is required to adapt to industry changes.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Can progress from junior programmer to senior programmer, CNC supervisor, or manufacturing engineer. With experience, can move into CAM software development or technical sales.

zh-CN.name: Embedded / Firmware Engineer
zh-CN.summary: Embedded/firmware engineers develop underlying software on microcontrollers and SoCs, covering RTOS/bare metal, drivers, communication protocol stacks, low power consumption, and firmware security, widely used in IoT, automotive, medical, and industrial equipment, making them high-value positions at the hardware and software intersection.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the United States, device networking and automotive/medical/defense electronics are driving embedded demand, with tight supply and demand for embedded/firmware engineers and a solid outlook.
zh-CN.trend_summary: Edge AI, functional safety, and device security have become hot topics in the US, with firmware engineers who understand low-level debugging and real-time constraints in short supply; AI-generated prototypes, but the hardware still relies on people at its core.

zh-CN.name: FPGA Engineer
zh-CN.summary: FPGA engineers use Verilog/VHDL to implement high-performance digital circuits on programmable logic devices, covering signal processing, low-latency computing, and hardware acceleration. They are mainly employed in defense aerospace, high-frequency trading, and semiconductor/telecommunications companies, where positions are scarce, barriers to entry, and salaries are attractive.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the United States, global chip autonomy and AI are accelerating the spillover of demand, FPGA engineers are scarce and even less available, senior talent is in short supply, and salaries are at the high end of electronic engineering platforms.
zh-CN.trend_summary: The US focuses on AI accelerators and low-power/simulation design, with engineers skilled in RTL, timing, and layout in a scarce position; AI assistance is limited, but architecture and tape-out responsibilities are highly professional.

These are scarce, high-threshold, and well-paid deep-tech positions.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the United States, global chip autonomy and AI demand are accelerating and spilling over, ASIC chip design engineers are scarce and even less available, while senior talent is in high demand and salaries are at the high end of electronic engineering.
zh-CN.trend_summary: The US focuses on AI accelerators and low-power/simulation design, with engineers skilled in RTL, timing, and layout in a scarce position; AI assistance is limited, but architecture and tape-out responsibilities are highly professional.

zh-CN.name: Analog / Mixed-Signal IC Design Engineer
zh-CN.summary: Analog/mixed-signal IC design engineers design analog and digital-analog hybrid modules in chips, such as ADC/DAC, PLL, power management (PMIC), RF front-end, and high-speed interfaces, which are recognized as the most difficult to automate and most rely on intuitive experience in chip design, with experts in extremely scarce.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the United States, global chip autonomy and AI are accelerating the spillover of demand, making analog/mixed-signal IC design engineers scarce and even less available, with senior talent in high demand and salaries at the high end of electronic engineering.
zh-CN.trend_summary: The US focuses on AI accelerators and low-power/simulation design, with engineers skilled in RTL, timing, and layout in a scarce position; AI assistance is limited, but architecture and tape-out responsibilities are highly professional.

zh-CN.name: IC Verification Engineer
zh-CN.summary: IC verification engineers use SystemVerilog/UVM to set up verification environments, write test platforms, and conduct coverage-driven and formal verification before chip tape-out, ensuring designs meet specifications. Verification workload usually accounts for more than half of chip development, with more positions than design positions, making it a relatively viable and high-paying path to enter the semiconductor industry.
zh-CN.forecast_note: In the United States, rising chip complexity drives up verification demand, and IC verification engineers typically outnumber design positions, making it a relatively viable high-paying path into semiconductors.
zh-CN.trend_summary: U.S. SoC-level verification, low power consumption, and security verification have become key priorities; AI improves test generation and debugging efficiency, while methodology and coverage convergence remain dominated by engineers.

zh-CN.trend_summary: Usually starts with an apprenticeship (4–5 years), progressing to journeyman, foreman, or supervisor. Experienced workers can move into inspection, project management, or entrepreneurship. Holding specialized welding certifications aids career development.

zh-CN.summary: Responsible for planning and managing catapults, arresting gear, and related mechanical, hydraulic, and control systems on aircraft carriers to ensure safe and efficient aircraft launch and recovery.
